newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday, with surging domestic A share markets making institutions borrow heavily in early-maturing contracts, traders said.
Tha annual rate for the most active three-day contract surged to 15.85 percent from 2.74 percent last Friday.
Turnover soared to 10.95 million lots from 3.76 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The repo market is linked to the A market performance," said one trader, "The surges in Shanghai and Shenzhen markets today absorbed much of its liquidity.
Traders said the issue today of Xinhua Metal Product Co, an A share firm, in Shanghai helped push the rates up. They expect rates to consolidate at high levels in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed, with five up and four down, in active trading.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, advanced to 117.00 yuan from 116.47 yuan. Traders expect the contracts to rise in the short term.
Volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.69 million lots from 2.45 million. - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
